# dokploy_schedule (Data Source)

Looks up a scheduled job of an application, a compose service or a server that already exists in Dokploy:

```terraform
data "dokploy_schedule" "cleanup" {
  service_id    = data.dokploy_application.web.id
  schedule_type = "application"
  name          = "cleanup"
}
```

A schedule of type `dokploy-server` has no parent. Look it up by `id`.

~> Dokploy does not enforce uniqueness for this record. If two schedule records match the lookup attributes, this data source fails instead of a guess. Look the record up by `id` in that case.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dokploy_schedule" "example" {
  id = "your-schedule-id"
}

data "dokploy_schedule" "cleanup" {
  service_id    = data.dokploy_application.web.id
  schedule_type = "application"
  name          = "cleanup"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Schedule id. Set it for a lookup by id, or leave it unset and set `service_id` with the distinguishing attributes.
- `name` (String) Display name of the schedule.
- `schedule_type` (String) Type of the parent: `application`, `compose`, `server` or `dokploy-server`.
- `service_id` (String) Id of the application, compose service or server that owns the schedule. Set it with `schedule_type` and `name`.

### Read-Only

- `app_name` (String) Internal name of the schedule.
- `command` (String) Command that the job runs.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp from the server.
- `cron_expression` (String) Cron expression of the schedule.
- `description` (String) Description of the job, or null.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the job runs.
- `script` (String) Script of the job, or null.
- `service_name` (String) Compose service name, or null.
- `shell_type` (String) Shell that runs the command: `bash` or `sh`.
- `timezone` (String) Time zone of the cron expression, or null.
